decisions.decision: Makers Fee quantity is the authoritative batch count
decisions.rationale: The Zoho catalog cannot identify a kit — all 516 items have a blank category and product_type 'goods'. The Makers Fee is charged once per fermentation slot; verified back to INV-000001 (Feb 2026: kit x3, fee x3). It caps every path, so batch count can never exceed what was paid for.

decisions.decision: Kit IDENTITY comes from the Kits sheet, not a price heuristic and not Zoho categories
decisions.rationale: The Kits sheet already IS a maintained registry (115 SKUs, 8 brands, stock/pricing/batch sizes; the admin panel reads it). It discriminates exactly where price could only guess, and fixes cases price got WRONG (a $40 cider kit beside a $300 fermenter). Tagging 516 Zoho items was considered and rejected as unnecessary.

decisions.decision: The kit registry may only ever NARROW candidates, never fall closed to zero
decisions.rationale: A kit added to Zoho but not yet to the Kits sheet must still get its batch. Silently losing a customer's batch is worse than mislabelling one. Falls back + warns; the fee cap still bounds the count.

decisions.decision: unit_total (not a unit_index column) for per-unit dedup in Apps Script
decisions.rationale: createBatch's appendRow is POSITIONAL, so a new column would require a live sheet schema migration. unit_total needs no schema change: the guard counts existing (invoice+SKU) rows and admits creates until unit_total exist. Retry-safety is preserved — once unit_total rows exist, further creates are duplicates again.

decisions.decision: Kit registry cached in module scope, refreshed hourly — NOT fetched per sale
decisions.rationale: createBatchesFromSale is fire-and-forget and must stay synchronous; making it async would have broken existing tests that assert axios calls synchronously (and CLAUDE.md forbids modifying existing tests).

decisions.decision: Corrected the existing INV-000137 test fixture (with explicit user approval)
decisions.rationale: It gave the Makers Fee quantity 1 alongside a kit quantity 3 — an invoice shape that has never existed (the real invoice has fee x3). Under the new cap it demanded 3 batches from 1 paid slot. Only the fixture changed; no assertion was weakened.

decisions.decision: Backfilled INV-000137 ONLY (2 batches), not all 9 affected invoices
decisions.rationale: User's call. An audit found 9 pre-fix invoices / 16 missing batches, but backfilling Feb-May orders would drop brand-new 'ready to start' batches into BrewPad for wine that was made and taken home months ago.

context_notes: Started as /gsd:resume-work, which audited Phase 56 and found it ~done. The session then pivoted to two live bugs the user raised: (1) the kiosk POS forcing an inventory reload after idle, and (2) INV-000137 showing only 1 batch in BrewPad when 3 kits were sold. Bug 2 unravelled into three separate defects, each hidden behind the last — the most important being that a fix committed on 2026-07-08 (fda6e40) had never actually worked in production because Apps Script's dedup guard silently rejected it. That was only discovered by ATTEMPTING the backfill against the live system; the code and its tests all looked correct. Biggest lesson of the session, recorded as an anti-pattern: a green test suite proved nothing about the deployed system, because the contradicting logic lived in Apps Script (not deployed by CI, no Jest harness). Second lesson: curl against prod returns a Cloudflare 403 bot-challenge page, which made me briefly conclude prod had NO GTM/CSP at all — prod must be verified through the browser.
